To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the citrus extract active packaging developed in this study complies with the OM limit for plastic materials in contact with food, the OM procedure in aqueous food simulant is not suitable, the citrus extract coating releases 75% of its antioxidant content into water and 12. 5% into oil, and the release decreases to 45 and to 25%, respectively, when the PET trays are plasma treated.
the migration of citrus extract from PET packaging is reduced when the PET is pretreated with a cold plasma, but this effect is lost when the citrus extract coating is applied.
the release of antioxidant compounds can be measured and subtracted from overall migration values in line with legislation, but the procedure for OM testing in aqueous simulants is not valid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of active packaging based on the incorporation of citrus extract in the coating of PET trays for the packaging of food.
the migration of antioxidant compounds from active packaging into food simulants and the development of a procedure for OM that is applicable to active packaging.
the overall migration and kinetics of the release of active compounds into food simulans of antioxidant active packaging prepared with plasma pretreated PET trays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plasma treatment of PET is a promising approach to enhance the performance of citrus extract coatings in active packaging.

the citrus extract-based antioxidant active packaging is safe and effective, and that the procedure of subtracting the released active compounds from the overall migration value is valid for solid food simulants.
the citrus extract coating was not suitable for the PET trays used in this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
citrus extract active coatings are a viable alternative to synthetic additives, with the added benefit of the release of natural antioxidant compounds.

plasma pretreatment of PET packaging is a promising technique to improve the release of antioxidant compounds, but further studies are required to optimize the pretreatment conditions and evaluate the impact of the treatment on the packaging.
the release of the citrus extract from the plasma treated and untreated PET trays was 75 and 45% into water and 12.6 and 25% in oil, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the migration of antioxidant compounds from an active packaging into food simulants can be measured to permit their removal from overall migration values, in accordance with the European Union regulation.
the migration of the antioxidant compounds from active packaging into food simulants is a complex phenomenon that requires a careful approach.

OM tests in aqueous food simulant may not provide accurate results for active packaging, and that a combination of OM and release tests may be necessary to ensure the safety of these packaging materials.
